title: Create Tailored Legal Agents with Agent Builder
format_note: Text-led feature film for Agent Builder: one serif headline per feature beat on the left, a simplified product panel on the right, closing on a black brand card.
one_thing: Harvey's Agent Builder lets legal teams run off-the-shelf or custom agents on a schedule, get notified, deploy them in chat and step in when asked.

transcript.voice_style: No speech. youtube_transcript found no caption track and local whisper returned only 'Music' for every segment.
transcript.script_shape: Eight on-screen headlines carry the whole script: name change, three feature claims, a notification beat, a deploy claim, a control claim, a quality claim, then a tagline.

good.observation: Each beat is one headline plus one UI moment, so a viewer reads a four-word claim while a cursor proves it. The pairing repeats six times with the same layout.
The Workflow Builder to Agent Builder rename is shown by striking one word through, not by explaining it. The change reads in under 2s.
The film names the product and gives the frame its subject inside the first 5s, with the wordmark on frame 0.
A full-frame banner, centred and alone, gives a single focal point right after the first hard cut and breaks a long run of split-screen beats.
The fade of line 2 from pale grey to black stages the headline in two reads without adding an accent colour or extra motion.
The closing inversion from white to black with a word-by-word tagline marks the end clearly and holds 3.3s.
Headline size stays in a narrow band across the film, 5.3-8.2% of frame height, so type reads as one system.

weak.observation: Result table and agent chat text are about 10 px tall at 1280 px wide, below the 2.6% type floor; the proof beats cannot be read at phone width.
'And Get Notified When Work Product is Done' has nine words and holds roughly 2.1s before the cut, under the reading rule.
Long stretches look static: 42% of sampled intervals are static and the longest static run is 6s, with no burst or climax in the cut rhythm.
True peak is -0.9 dBTP, 0.1 dB over the -1 dBTP ceiling, with integrated loudness at -13.9 LUFS.

rule_candidates.rule: A calm explainer can run on in-shot change instead of cuts: two hard cuts in 40s, median shot 17.76s, but a new headline or UI state every 3-4s.
A burst of 5-8 cuts is not needed for a feature explainer; this film has no burst and lands its hero moment at 50% of runtime with a single hard cut.
Set a two-line headline with line 1 in full black and line 2 in pale grey that darkens to black over about 0.5s, as the second-line accent instead of one accent word.
Show a product rename as a strikethrough on the old word followed by the new name, within 2s, so the problem is shown and not captioned.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0002.jpg at t=2s, f0003.jpg at t=4s

rule_candidates.rule: Keep the headline fixed while the right-hand UI changes: the title on the left stays still across 3-5s holds while cards, form values and chat lines update.
Any UI line the viewer must read should be at least 19 px tall on a 720 px frame (2.6%); crop or zoom the UI rather than showing a full table at about 10 px.
End a light film with a hard cut to a black card and build the tagline word by word at about 0.12-0.16s a word, then hold the finished line and logo about 3s.
A light film with grey UI panels uses a single full-frame dark element as its hero, placed at the middle of the runtime, to break the split-screen pattern.
